title: Conformance & regression harness for streaming, function-calls, structured outputs, and compatibility
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Build a repeatable conformance and regression test harness that covers: 1) streaming endpoints (chunk ordering, metadata events, end-of-stream markers), 2) tool/function-calling contract (argument shapes, required/optional keys, error modes), 3) structured JSON/YAML outputs (schema conformance, recoverable parse errors), and 4) compatibility layers (older client payloads, legacy param names). The harness must support golden prompts per model/version, deterministic execution when possible, and fail-fast CI integration that gates merges on API compatibility regressions. The implementation will include contract tests (request/response shapes + headers), golden-prompt regression suites (assertions on canonical outputs or normalized structure), and CI jobs that produce artifact diffs and a stability score per model/version.
acceptance_criteria: CI job 'api-conformance' runs on every PR and nightly on main producing a pass/fail and an artifact bundle with diffs
Golden prompt suite: 120 prompts covering streaming, function-calling, structured output across at least 3 model families (open-llama-7b, redwood-small, redwood-verified-1.0)
Contract tests that validate HTTP semantics: multi-part streaming boundaries, content-type + content-encoding, and required response headers
Mock tool runner that verifies function calling payloads reach downstream services and simulates common error modes (timeout, 4xx validation, 5xx retryable)
Backward-compat tests that exercise legacy client keys (e.g., 'model_id' vs 'model') and automatic compatibility layer mapping
Fail-on-regression policy: >5% structural assertion failures across golden prompts blocks merge; exceptions must be approved and documented
Security review sign-off recorded on the ticket and tests do not log sensitive prompt text unredacted in CI artifacts
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Malik: Kickoff spike completed. Spent 2 days enumerating failure modes for streaming (partial-chunk loss, out-of-order chunks under TCP retransmit), and collected an initial set of 60 golden prompts from product/solutions. Decided we need deterministic seeding for models when asserting token-level outputs — but for structured outputs we'll normalize via JSON schema and canonicalization.

2026-03-04 - Diego Romero: Built first prototype for streaming contract test using a lightweight harness that replays recorded HTTP chunk sequences. Prototype catches a bug where 'end_of_stream' metadata event was omitted when the model returned an empty final chunk — filed ENG-4742 to fix runtime behavior.

2026-03-06 - Eleanor Park (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria; requested coverage for function-calls edge cases: missing optional args, additional unknown args, and nested object args. Also asked for a small set of customer-facing examples to include in the public docs X: https://confluence.redwood/company/api/golden-prompts

2026-03-08 - Samir Patel (Design): UX feedback on error payloads from structured outputs. Prefer a 'parse_context' object in responses when output parsing fails to assist client-side recovery. Added to contract proposals and mock runner behavior.

2026-03-10 - Diego Romero: Implemented JSON-schema based validator for structured outputs. It supports 'recoverable' and 'fatal' violation levels. Added canonicalization layer that sorts object keys and strips metadata fields before comparing to golden outputs.

2026-03-12 - Lena Zhou (Reliability): Requested telemetry hooks in tests to surface flaky streaming patterns (latency distribution per chunk, retransmits, partial-chunk counts). Added a metrics producer that the CI job uploads to the observability test namespace.

2026-03-13 - Security review (Marta Iverson): Flagged that golden prompts may contain customer PII when teams add real examples. Action: add a redaction step in CI that masks emails, API keys, and long digit sequences and produce an audit report. Security sign-off required before main-nightly promotion.

2026-03-14 - Diego Romero: Merged initial harness into feature branch. CI job defined in .github/workflows/api-conformance.yml producing artifacts at ./build/api-conformance/$GIT_SHA. Next: increase prompt set to 120 and wire up model matrix for dedicated/private deployments. Open questions: how to represent nondeterministic token choices for sampling models in golden tests (proposal: use structure-only assertions or token-set membership checks)
notes: Trade-offs: strict token-level golden assertions are brittle across model patches and quantization changes; prioritized structured-output and contract assertions as first-class guards. For streaming we'll maintain both sequence-level checks and heuristics for chunk timing but avoid flakiness by recording and replaying chunk sequences in CI in a controlled environment.
next_steps: 1) Expand golden prompt corpus to 120 prompts and tag prompts by feature area (streaming, tool-calls, structured). 2) Wire harness to run against dedicated and private deployments in staging. 3) Add a CI gate that blocks merges when nightly stability score for a model-family drops more than 3 points. 4) Document maintenance process for golden prompts and include owners per prompt.
